IV.  HOSPITALS  AND  DISPENSARIES 
ALL  INDIA  INSTITUTE  OF  AYURVEDA,  NEW DELHI 
 
4.1.1   A state-of-the-art All India Institute of  Ayurveda is being set up at New Delhi to 
provide quality patient care services under th e Ayurvedic System of Medicine.  The 
Institute once operational would facilitate quality research ai med at bridging gaps in the 
scientific information about quality, safe ty and efficacy of Ayurveda products and 
developing benchmarks of Ayurvedic education, research and health care. 
4.1.2 The Committee notes that against the Eleventh Plan Outlay of Rs.150.00 crore, 
only Rs.45.00 crore could be releas ed during the first  three y ears of the Plan period and 
the actual expenditure level till 15th March, 2010 is  Rs.11.74 crore.  The Committee also 
notes that the capital cost of the project as approved by the Cabinet is Rs.134.00 crore. 
 
4.1.3 The Committee has been monitoring the progress being made in the setting up of 
the All India Institute of Ayurveda in Ne w Delhi.  This ambitious project although 
conceptualized much before the beginning of the Eleventh Plan continues to remain on 
paper inspite of only two years remaining for the Plan period to end.  Track-record of 
progress made so far has been very discour aging.  After completi on of the preparatory 
exercise, EFC gave its approval on 9 th May, 2007.  Thereafter, it took more than one and 
a half years to get the Cabinet approval in January, 2008.  It took anot her year in getting 
M/s HSCC (India) Ltd. appointed as the Consultant for the project.  The Committee finds 
that the only progress made during  2009-10 is payment of advance of Rs.4.50 crore to 
the contractor through  HSCC.  In reply to a query regarding the present status of the 
Institute, the Department has informed that there is no change in the estimates of the 
project which is expected to be completed within two years from the date of 
commencement of construction viz. May, 2010. 

 
4.1.4 The Committee is happy to note the subm ission of the Department that there 
is no change in the estimates of the projec t and the project is on track and expected 
to be completed within two years from the date of commencement of construction, 
i.e., May 2010.  However, more than tw o years have already elapsed since the 
Cabinet approved the project in Janua ry, 2008 but the designs and plan of 
construction of the project are yet to be approved by the Delhi Development 
Authority (DDA).   Therefore, the constr uction of the building scheduled to 
commence in 2009-10 itself has been rescheduled for May, 2010.  
4.1.5 The Committee observes that it is impera tive on the part of the Department to 
vigorously pursue approval of designs and drawings of the building with the DDA at 
the highest level.   The Committee also  recommends that the progress of the 
construction of the building be monitored  at a sufficiently higher level in the 
Department so that no room is left for time overruns and the resultant cost 
overruns. 
 
CGHS  AYURVEDA  HOSPITAL,  NEW DELHI.
 
 
4.2.1   Eleventh Plan outlay for the CGHS Ayurveda Hospital, New Delhi was Rs. 6.50 
crore.  During the first thre e years of the Plan period, only Rs. 2.20 crore was released 
and upto 15 th March, 2010, expenditure reported is only Rs.19 lakhs.  The Committee 
notes that no provision for the hospital is proposed for 2010-11. 
 
4.2.2     On a specific query about the latest status of upgradation of CGHS 
Ayurveda Hospital from 25 to 50 bedded hospital, the Committee has been informed 
that major renovation and repair work of the hospital building has been completed.  
However, the work relating to Operati on Theatre and Panchkarma Therapy 
sections etc. is being pursued.  The Co mmittee wonders at what stage is this 
exercise, as funds duly allocated are going unutilized. 
 
4.2.3   Another area of concern for the Committ ee is the non-filling up of required 
(52) posts of Ayurvedic doctors and para -medicals required for upgradation of the 

Hospital.  The Committee finds that only 20 Ayurvedic Medical Officers have joined 
so far.  The Committee is not aware about the status of para-medical personnel.  
Posts of Medical Superintendent of the Hosp ital is yet to be filled.  In such a 
scenario, the Committee can only conclude  that the CGHS Ayurveda Hospital 
cannot be considered fully functional as the Ho spital is yet to be equipped with both 
required infrastructure and manpower.  The Committee once again enjoins upon 
the Department to make all efforts so as to ensure the outreach of envisaged health 
care to the targeted beneficiaries. 
 
 EXPANSION OF AYUSH SYSTEM UNDER CGHS 
 
4.3.1    Against Eleventh Plan outlay of Rs.6.30 crore for expansion of AYUSH System 
under CGHS, expenditure reported upto 15 th March, 2010  is only Rs.1.47 crore.  
Provision of Rs.1.30 crore has been proposed for 2010-11.   
4.3.2    The AYUSH component was introduced in CGHS by opening of one 
Ayurvedic Dispensary way back in 1964.  Si nce then, very few AYUSH dispensaries 
have been set up under CGHS.  The Commi ttee finds that there has not been any 
worthwhile progress in this direction so fa r.  Things are rather deteriorating.  This 
is borne out by the fact that against the Eleventh Plan target of opening of 21 
AYUSH  dispensaries under CGHS which were sanctioned during the Tenth Plan 
period, not even a single dispensary could be established during the first three years 
of the Eleventh Plan.  The Committee finds it very disturbing that a modest 
beginning of establishment of Ayurveda  dispensaries at Delhi, Kanpur and 
Chandigarh, Homoeopathy dispensaries at Jabalpur and Bhopal and  a Unani 
dispensary at Bhopal remains on paper.   Reason given is more astounding i.e., 
inability to create the required posts. 
 
4.3.3    The Committee takes note of Mi d-term Assessment of Eleventh Plan 
whereby it has been emphasized to pr ovide AYUSH facilities in 10 CGHS 
dispensaries by the end of Eleventh Plan (2011-12).  For this purpose, required posts 
need to be created on top priority basis and filled up also immediately thereafter.

that the total cost of the first phase of the project is estimated at Rs.67.50 crore.  The

2009-10 and proposed provision of Rs .17.00 crore for 2010-11, one can draw the 
very obvious conclusion.  The Committee apprehends that  chances of there being 
both time-overruns and cost-overruns a re very much there.  The Committee can 
only emphasize that the Task Force has to  vigorously supervise the implementation 
of first phase of NEIAH at Shillong, id entifying the problem areas along with

VI. RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT  
 
6.1 The four Research Councils, viz (i) Cent ral Council for Research in Ayurveda and 
Siddha (CCRAS); (ii) Central Council for Re search in Unani Medi cine (CCRUN) (iii) 
Central Council for Research in Homoe opathy (CCRH) and (iv) Central Council for 
Research in Yoga and Naturopathy (CCRYN) ar e the apex bodies for scientific research 
in the concerned systems of medicine.  The research activities of the Research Councils 
are monitored and reviewed periodically in orde r to ensure that the research is focused 
and that it is undertaken in a time bound manner.  The out puts of the research studies are 
disseminated among educationists, research ers, physicians, manufacturers and the 
common man. 
 
6.2 The Committee was informed that these Councils of the Department have played 
a major role in the field of research.  The Committee is happy to note that based on the 
Nityanand Committee recommendations, a numb er of measures have been taken for 
reorganization of CCRAS, upgradation of it s institutes and labo ratories. Dr. Qazi 
Committee on CCRUM is expected to submit it s report shortly.  The existing guidelines 
of Extra Mural Research scheme are under revision to consider raising the maximum 
limit of the grant admissible per project from Rs.30 lakhs to Rs. 2 crores. 
 
6.3 The Committee observes that a large num ber of research projects covering vital 
areas of healthcare are being handled by the Research Councils.  Out of the very wide 
range of ongoing /completed research projects, some of the very prominent ones are – 
- safety studies on 8 herbo-metallic formulations completed under GTP  
- Pre-clinical studies on 8 formulati ons relating to 4 di sease conditions 
completed 
- AYUSH QOL – 2A for HIV AIDS-pre-clinical trials completed by 
CCRAS/ICMR 
- International collaborative studies – osteoarthritis and Anxiety Neurosis 
with Charite University,  Chronic Fatigue Syndrome with Mayo Clinic, 
Meta analysis of Ayurveda Research  with SAMA (Switzerland) 

- CCRAS/CCRUM/CCRH research proj ects with AIIMS, NIMHANS, 
BARG, Bose Trust, RML, BHU, St.Johns Medical College, Bangalore 
- Drug standardization in Psoriasis,  Malaria, Hepatitis, Osteoporosis, 
Filariasis, Sickle Cell anemia etc. 
 
 The Committee also takes note of ongoing research for development of 17 
Ayurvedic and 16 Siddha drugs of Antenata l, Neonatal and Post natal care and their 
introduction under the Reproductive and child health services. 
6.4  As per the information made availabl e to the Committee against the projected 
demand, of Rs.70.00 crore for CCRAS and Rs.33.39 crore for CCRUM for 2010-11, plan 
allocation is Rs.59.00 crore and Rs.30.39 crore respectively.  Explaining the adverse 
effect of the reduced allocation vis-à-vis pr ojected demand, the De partment has stated 
that collaborative research projects with inte rnational institutions require a higher degree 
of funding as international costs of conducting pa rallel trials abroad are very high.  This 
has hindered partnerships for quality research overseas.  At the same time this is the need 
of the times as traditional systems are in creasingly being confr onted on the lack of 
adequate scientific validation globally. 
 
6.5 The Committee concurs with the views of  the Department and observes that 
under-funding may impact adversely on th e quality of research activities of the 
Research Councils.  The Committee notes from  the information furn ished to it that 
both CCRAS and CCRUM have shown excel lent track record in utilizing the 
budgeted funds in 2009-10.  Again, the plan allocation of Rs.59.00 crore in 2009-10, 
the CCRAS utilized Rs.58.13 crore till 15
th March, 2010.  Similarly, CCRUM 
utilized Rs.8.21 crore till that date agains t the Plan provision of Rs.11.00 crore for 
2009-10.  Keeping in view, the above facts the Committee recommends that higher 
allocation be made for CCRAS and CCRUM at R.E. stage.  The Committee is of the 
considered view that there is an urgent n eed to step up research investments for the 
development of ASU&H drugs and colla borative research with reputed 
international institutions will go a long wa y in validating the health benefits of 
ASU&H drugs. 
6.6   Committee’s attention has been drawn by some reports about successful 
treatment of Cancer patients by Ayurvedic drugs.  On a specific query about the 

veracity of these reports, the Committee was pleasantly surprised to note the 
significant achievements made by the Ayurvedic practitioners as indicated below:- 
- On the recommendation of the Scient ific Advisory Committee (Ayurveda), 
the CCRAS has initiated the study of  ‘CARCTOL’ a proprietary medicine 
of Vaid Nand Lal Tiwari of Jaipur supposed to have anti-cancer properties.  
For verifying the therapeutic claim,  standardization work has been 
completed by the Council.  Safety and toxicity studies have also been 
completed.  As informed by the Ex. Director-General, CCRAS, 
‘CARCTOL’ has also been subjected to in-vitro study at Advanced Cancer  
Research  Centre of TATA, Mumbai against 14 types of human cancer cells 
out of which it was found effective agains t pancreatic and lung cancer.  It 
was placed on record that CARCTOL is being used for treatment of cancer 
patients both in the country and ab road.  After preparation of dossiers, 
multi-centric clinical trials will be conducted. 
 
- Pre-clinical study of ‘Cancer Gaza Kesari’ a proprietary drug of Vaid 
Krishan Gopal of Ajmer has also been conducted by the Council in 
collaboration with Veterinary College,  Chennai.  The study revealed that 
the drug significantly reduced the mammary tumour incidence, latency, 
frequency, rate of growth and malignancy.  It was also subjected to in-vitro 
study against 14 types of human cancer cell line, out of which it has shown 
to be of effect against Pancreatic and Lung Cancer. 
 
-  Pilot project was sanctioned by the Ministry in 1996 to study the effects of 
metal based formulations prepared by  Vaid Balendu Prakash of Dehradun 
in the treatment of Acute pro-myllo lic Leukemia.  The Committee was 
informed that the drug was patented jointly by the Council with Germany.  
The Committee was also given to und erstand the Vaid Balendu Prakash 
has been treating Cancer patients with  the drug.On a specific query it was 
clarified that the Indo-German patent was a process patent.  So far only a 
pilot study of 21 patients has been conducted by the Council. Multi-
Cultural Clinical Trials of the dr ug were to be undertaken which would 
take four years. 
 
- The Committee also notes that ethical approval and release of funds for 
clinical trial of AYUSH QOL-2C at AIIMS has been completed.  
Registration of patent is to be init iated shortly. Simultaneously, 10 patients 
have been enrolled for study at St. Johns  Medical College, Bangalore.  This 
drug is reported to improve quality of life of those receiving 
chemotherapy/radiotherapy. 
 
6.7 The Committee places on record its appreciation of commendable work 
being done by the Research Councils on th eir own and also in collaboration with 
well-known institutions in the country a nd abroad.  Work of the CCRAS touches 

both routine ailments as well as chronic ailments where permanent cure is yet to be 
found inspite of giant strides made by th e modern medical scie nces.  In such a 
scenario, for the treatment of the most deadly cancer disease, any significant 
achievement by any system of medicine sh ould be welcome to all.  The Committee 
considers it a strange irony that although large number of patients are getting relief 
by the drugs formulated by individuals a fter years of their single-handed research, 
official recognition still remains elusive to them.  The Committee strongly advocates 
the streamlining and expediting of the official certification process, so that humanity 
at large gets the long-awaited relief.

 IX   QUALITY CONTROL  OF  AYUSH  DRUGS
 
 
9.1 The AYUSH system of medicine is gove rned by Drugs & Cosmetics Act, 1940 
and Rules made there under.  Enforcement provision of Chapter IV A of drugs & 
Cosmetics Act, 1940 is a responsibility of St ate Governments.  Establishment of state 
Drug Testing Laboratories is also a statutory responsibility of States under the Act.  To 
provide financial assistance to States for strengthening enforcement mechanism, the Drug 
Quality control scheme was started in IXth pl an.  Over the years, 29 state drug testing 
laboratories and 46 state pharmacies  have been set up and upgraded @ Rs.1.50 
crore/DTL and Rs. 2.00 crore/pharmacy.  In the Eleventh plan the scheme was revised to 
include three new components of strengthening  of the state   enforcement mechanism, 
upgrading the in-house testing facilities of manufacturing un its and assisting 
manufacturing units desirous of obtaining higher GMP like EU and WHO-GMP. 
9.2   The Committee notes that inspite of ma jor changes in the scheme, fund utilization 
status has been far from satisfactory.  Agains t an Eleventh Plan outlay of Rs.225 crore, 
funds amounting to only Rs. 45.00 crore could be allocated during the first three years of 
the plan period and expenditure reported upto 15th March, 2010 is only Rs.26.52 crore.   
9.3 The Committee finds that out of 29 Drug Tes ting laboratories assisted financially so 
far, 17 labs are established in terms of e quipment and buildings.  Other labs are in 
different stages of construc tion of building and procuremen t of equipment.   Only 46 
ASU&H pharmacies have been covered under the scheme so far. 
9.4   Committee’s attention has also been  drawn by the very low number of GMP 
compliant ASU&H Drug manufacturing units in  the country.  Out of total 9837 such 
units only 4663 units are GMP complying uni ts.  Ratio of GMP compliant /non-GMP 
compliant  units is very unsatisfactory wi th the maximum gap noticed in States like 

Assam, Haryana, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, U.P., Tamil Nadu, Uttarakhand, 
Punjab.  As many as 2336 legal notices have been issued/licenses cancelled so far.   
9.5  The Committee has taken note of a num ber of corrective measures suggested 
during the mid-term appraisal of Eleven th plan.  The Committee would like to 
emphasize that quality control and quality assurance are the major issues with 
reference to ASU drugs.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that corrective 
measures as suggested in the mid-term appraisal may be initiated without delay. 
 
 
9.6 The Committee also takes note of the fact that the rules regarding proper 
labeling on Ayurvedic, Siddha, Unani and Homoeopathic (ASU & H) drugs are not 
being complied with strictly.  The Commi ttee feels that the absence of proper 
labeling on ASU & H drugs may be a caus e of health hazards.  The Committee 
therefore, recommends that the monito ring mechanism in this regard be 
streamlined to ensure proper labeling on ASU & H drugs.

- On the recommendation of the Scient ific Advisory Committee (Ayurveda), 
the CCRAS has initiated the study of  ‘CARCTOL’ a proprietary medicine 
of Vaid Nand Lal Tiwari of Jaipur supposed to have anti-cancer properties.  
For verifying the therapeutic claim,  standardization work has been 
completed by the Council.  Safety and toxicity studies have also been 
completed.  As informed by the Ex. Director-General, CCRAS, 
‘CARCTOL’ has also been subjected to in-vitro study at Advanced Cancer  
Research  Centre of TATA, Mumbai against 14 types of human cancer cells 
out of which it was found effective agains t pancreatic and lung cancer.  It 
was placed on record that CARCTOL is being used for treatment of cancer 

patients both in the country and ab road.  After preparation of dossiers, 
multi-centric clinical trials will be conducted. 
 
- Pre-clinical study of ‘Cancer Gaza Kesari’ a proprietary drug of Vaid 
Krishan Gopal of Ajmer has also been conducted by the Council in 
collaboration with Veterinary College,  Chennai.  The study revealed that 
the drug significantly reduced the mammary tumour incidence, latency, 
frequency, rate of growth and malignancy.  It was also subjected to in-vitro 
study against 14 types of human cancer cell line, out of which it has shown 
to be of effect against Pancreatic and Lung Cancer. 
 
-  Pilot project was sanctioned by the Ministry in 1996 to study the effects of 
metal based formulations prepared by  Vaid Balendu Prakash of Dehradun 
in the treatment of Acute pro-myllo lic Leukemia.  The Committee was 
informed that the drug was patented jointly by the Council with Germany.  
The Committee was also given to und erstand the Vaid Balendu Prakash 
has been treating Cancer patients with  the drug.On a specific query it was 
clarified that the Indo-German patent was a process patent.  So far only a 
pilot study of 21 patients has been conducted by the Council. Multi-
Cultural Clinical Trials of the dr ug were to be undertaken which would 
take four years. 
 
- The Committee also notes that ethical approval and release of funds for 
clinical trial of AYUSH QOL-2C at AIIMS has been completed.  
Registration of patent is to be init iated shortly. Simultaneously, 10 patients 
have been enrolled for study at St. Johns  Medical College, Bangalore.  This 
drug is reported to improve quality of life of those receiving 
chemotherapy/radiotherapy. (Para 6.6) 
 
 The Committee places on record its appreciation of commendable work 
being done by the Research Councils on th eir own and also in collaboration with 
well-known institutions in the country a nd abroad.  Work of the CCRAS touches 
both routine ailments as well as chronic ailments where permanent cure is yet to be 
found inspite of giant strides made by th e modern medical scie nces.  In such a 
scenario, for the treatment of the most deadly cancer disease, any significant 
achievement by any system of medicine sh ould be welcome to all.  The Committee 
considers it a strange irony that although large number of patients are getting relief 
by the drugs formulated by individuals a fter years of their single-handed research, 
official recognition still remains elusive to them.  The Committee strongly advocates 
the streamlining and expediting of the official certification process, so that humanity 
at large gets the long-awaited relief.  (Para 6.7) 

 
VII.  MAINSTREAMING  OF  AYUSH  INSTITUTIONS  UNDER    NRHM 
 
 
 The Committee observes that one of th e major initiatives of the Department 
i.e., the mainstreaming  of AYUSH institutions and pr actitioners in the National 
Health Care delivery System inspite of be ing revised is clouded with a number of 
constraints. The Committee is  convinced that AYUSH – syst em of health care is a 
viable alternative to the allopathic line of treatmen t as it has a number of 
comparative strengths including a holistic approach, personalized system of care, 
fewer side effects, affordability and accessibility etc. The Committee, accordingly, 
strongly recommends that required funds along with other infrastructure, staff etc.   
be provided to the Department for this im portant  initiative.  The Committee also 
emphathises with the Department to ma ke use of available funds and resources 
optimally and judiciously. (Para 7.5) 
 
VIII NATIONAL  MEDICINAL  PLANTS  BOARD
 
 
The Committee has been voicing its concern about the problem areas noticed 
in the running of erstwhile Promotional and Contractual Farming Schemes of the 
Board.  The main area of concern was ava ilability of the unspent balances with the 
implementation agencies.  As per the latest information made available to the 
Committee, 4143 Utilisation C ertifificates amounting to  Rs.56.21 crore are pending 
as on 4.3.2010.  Pendency status in the following states is quite alarming: 
(Rs. in crores) 
State No. of UCs Amount 
Karnataka 427 6.49 
MP 444 5.79 
Maharashtra 424 5.02 
Rajasthan 1398 10.05 
       (Para 8.4) 
 
 
                                                              

 The Committee, accordingly, recommends to the Department to take 
corrective measures on an urgent basi s to address the inherent problem areas 
hampering the schemes and also impress upo n the States and State Medicinal Plant 
Boards for timely submission of UCs.  (Para 8.7) 
 The Committee has been constantly drawing the attention of the Department 
to the organizational set up of the National  Medicinal Plants Board.  Although as 
per the Department, the Board is fully func tional at present, the details of the 
officers /staff in position is  self revealing.  Out of 14 regular officers/staff, 6 staff 
members are posted on temporary basis from different councils of the Department.  
There are as many as 22 contractual consultants/outsourced staff working in the 
Board.  The Committee finds the present st atus of filling up of posts created for the 
Board very disturbing.  11 posts, out of which 10 posts were created in 2007 and 1 in 
2004, are lying vacant.  What is more worrisome is that these posts include the posts 
of CEO, Director Technical, Dy. Director (Medicinal Plants), Manager (Marketing 
and Trade), Finance Administrative Of ficer, Research Officer (Medicinal 
Plants/Agronomy).  The Committee also no tes that some of the posts are lying 
vacant as suitable candidates are simply  not available inspite of the Department 
advertising again and again.  Taking a seri ous view of status of manpower at the 
National Medicinal Plants Board, the Committee once again urges upon the 
Department to make all conceivable effort s for getting the vacant posts filled up.  
The Committee would like to point out that  mere launching of ambitious schemes, 
followed by their substantive revision after a short interval will not serve the 
purpose.  Simultaneous availability of required manpower is equally important. 
(Para 8.8) 
 The Committee would also appreciat e if exercise for reviewing the 
structuring of the State B oards is also undertaken by  the Department so that 
problem areas notice therein can also be removed. (Para 8.9) 
 
 

 IX   QUALITY CONTROL  OF  AYUSH  DRUGS 
 
   
 The Committee has taken note of a num ber of corrective measures suggested 
during the mid-term appraisal of Eleven th plan.  The Committee would like to 
emphasize that quality control and quality assurance are the major issues with 
reference to ASU drugs.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that corrective 
measures as suggested in the mid-term a ppraisal may be initiated without delay. 
(Para 9.5) 
 
 The Committee also takes note of the fact that the rules regarding proper 
labeling on Ayurvedic, Siddha, Unani and Homoeopathic (ASU & H) drugs are not 
being complied with strictly.  The Commi ttee feels that the absence of proper 
labeling on ASU & H drugs may be a caus e of health hazards.  The Committee 
therefore, recommends that the monito ring mechanism in this regard be 
streamlined to ensure proper labeling on ASU & H drugs. (Para 9.6) 
 
X.   AYUSH  PHARMACEUTICAL  INDUSTRY
 
 
INDIAN  MEDICINE  PHARMACEUTICAL  CORPORATION  LIMITED    
(IMPCL) 
 
The Committee observes that this is th e only Government enterprise which 
through its wide range of products has been playing a major role in the propagation 
of AYUSH system of healthcare.  The Co mmittee, however fails  to understand the 
reasons for not releasing any funds to the Corporation from Rs.5.00 crore provided 
for the Eleventh Plan.   It is, but natu ral that all the required support is made 
available both for infrastructure and manpo wer so that IMPCL continues to carry 
out its mandated task.  The Committee ma y also be kept informed about the 3
rd 
phase of modernization which is underw ay at the Corporation.  The Committee 
would also appreciate if concrete steps are taken to enlarge the area of open market 
sales of the products being manufactured at IMPCL. (Para 10.3) 
 

XI. DEVELOPMENT  OF  COMMON  FACILITIES  FOR THE AYUSH  
INDUSTRY  CLUSTERS 
 
The Committee observes that plan a llocation of Rs. 25.00 crore in 2009-10 
was brought down to Rs.10.00 crore  at the RE stage as on 15 th March, 2010 
utilisation status was Rs.8.57 crore.  Th e Committee was informed that the 
allocation was curtailed due to reduced a llocation as  a whole for the Department 
and as a result, request for second inst allment could not be  fully met  The 
Committee finds that against the projec ted requirement of Rs.50.00 crore for 2010-
11 Rs.25.00 crore has been allocated.  The Co mmittee  recommends that in view of 
the absorption capacity of funds of the scheme, the allocation may be suitably  
enhanced. (Para 11.2) 
 
XII.   SURVEY  ON  USAGE  AND  ACCEPTABILITY  OF  AYUSH
 
 
  
 The Committee observes that  the survey has been continuing as a proposal 
stage from the Tenth Plan. When asked to clarify the reasons therefor, the 
Committee was informed that the delay in undertaking the survey was mainly due 
to finalization of an agency/institution having capacity and competence for 
conducting nation-wide household survey.  Latest position is that the National 
Sample Survey Organization (NSSO) has be en requested to undertake the survey 
for AYUSH along with their Socio-Economic  Survey.  In the me antime, the Health 
Department has also been requested to includ e this item in the ne xt National Health 
and Family Welfare Survey. (Para 12.2) 
 
The Committee fails to understand the reason for undue delay in the 
finalization of an agency for undertak ing such a vital issue of usage and 
acceptability of AYUSH.  The Committee wo nders as to how funds amounting to 
Rs.66 lakhs could be spent when an agency fo r the survey is yet to be finalized.   
Both the surveys by NSSO and National Health and Family Welfare  Survey are 

being conducted since long.  It would be in the fitness of things if modalities for the 
survey are expedited prior to survey.  The findings emerging from the data collected 
though survey would prove to be of imme nse help in formulat ion of    future 
strategies for AYUSH. (Para 12.3) 
 
XIII   DEVELOPMENT  OF  INSTITUTIONS
 
 
 
 The Committee observes that agains t Eleventh Plan Outlay or Rs.550.00 
crore for development of Educational Instit utions, funds released during the first 
three years of the plan period amount ed to only Rs.157.00 crore and expenditure 
reported upto 15th March, 2010 was only Rs.102.04 crore.  The Committee finds that 
the position has been very discouraging  during the last two years as indicated 
below: 
(Rs. in Crores) 
2008-09 2009-10 
BE RE Actuals BE RE Actuals 
(Upto 15.3.10) 
65.00 36.71 40.00 45.00 20.00 18.67 
 
Not only this, achievement level of phy sical targets has also been showing a 
downward trend.  Against 38 and 20 institutions targeted to be assisted during 2008-
09 and 2009-10, only 32 and 11 institutio ns could be assisted respectively. 
Pending/incomplete Utilization Certificates, slow pace of Utilization and lack of 
adequate number of fresh proposals have b een cited as the main factors responsible 
for this slow pace of utilization. (Para 13.3) 
 
The Committee was given to understand that changes are proposed in the 
eligibility criteria for releasing grants-i n-aid to AYUSH Educational Institutions.  
Increase in the quantum of grants in-aid for infrastructural development, changes 
in the Central/State and Centre/private institution funding pattern are being 
finalized.  The Committee hopes that fina lization of all these changes will be 
expedited.  One must not forget that good quality education in all AYUSH systems 

of medicine is the very foundation for propagation of these age-old traditional 
systems of health care, very much required for our country. (Para 13.4) 
XIV   PUBLIC HEALTH \INITIATIVES  
  The Committee strongly feels that such  initiatives need to be sustained and 
expanded across the country.  All conceivable efforts therefore need to be taken in 
this direction. (Para 14.2) 
XV.  INTERNATIONAL COOPERATION 
 The Committee observes that at internat ional level also, the Department has 
been coming forward with tie-up with countries like China, Russia, SAARC Group 
of Nations and ASEAN Countries.  However, along with such init iatives, there is a 
growing need for validation of both the AYU SH systems and products on scientific 
lines in the wake of growing global concerns in this regard.  Setting up of an Indo-
US Centre for Research on Indian System of Medicine (CRISM) in the University of 
Mississippi, USA is a step in the right dir ection.  The Committee hopes that such a 
move along with joint centres with national  level medical and scientific institutions 
would go a long way in establishing the validity and efficacy of AYUSH system of 
healthcare. (Para 15.1) 
 Lastly, the Committee welcomes the setting up of an Advisory Committee 
under the Chairmanship of Dr. R.A.  Mashelkar on various issues on the 
International cooperation sector which will also play a pivotal role.  (Para 15.2)

REPORT 
I. INTRODUCTION 
 
1.1 The Department of Health Research was created in the Ministry of Health and 
Family Welfare in 2007 and be came functional in November, 2008 with appointment of the 
first Secretary, who is also DG, ICMR. 
 
1.2 Department of Health Research (DHR) aims  at bringing modern health technology 
to people by encouraging innovations related to diagnostics, treatment methods as well as 
prevention- vaccines; translating the innovations into products/processes  by facilitating 
evaluation/testing in synergy with other Dep artments of Ministry of Health and Family 
Welfare as well as other Departments engaged in health research and introducing these 
innovations into public health service through health systems research.  
  
1.3 The Committee has been given to understand that there are very few laboratories 
apart from National Institute of Virology (N IV) and National Centre for Disease Control 
(NCDC) which are engaged in health research.  Health research is confined to a handful of 
medical colleges as the remaining medical colleges lack requisite infrastructure and 
manpower for conducting research.  Also, th ere are negligible incentives available for 
conducting medical research.  The Secretary, Health Research informed the Committee that 
the following major schemes are envisaged for augmentation of infrastructure and 
manpower. 
 
a) Creation of Network of Laboratories for Viral Diagnosis 
 
Proposal to set up four categories of laboratories across the country: 
• National Institute of Communicable Diseases (NICD) and NIV to be 
 national reference centres, (BSL-IV facilities) 
• Grade I laboratories (28): Reference Centre for Each State (BSL-III facilities) 
• Grade II laboratories (60): Equipped with BSL2 
• Grade III laboratories (80): 
 
b) Special support to the medical colleges: 
• Assistance for setting up advanced centres on various aspects of  

 7
      medicine in different institutions/places 
                Establishing  
• Modern biology units. 
• Advanced centres in selected medical colleges in a phased manner. 
 
c) Establishment of Model  Rural Health Research Units 
 
Proposal to: 
• establish infrastructure at the new model rural health research units, 
• strengthen the existing units 
• set up training facilities for doctors and other health care personnel on 
diagnosis, treatment & epidemiology at these units. 
 
1.4     The Committee appreciates the efforts made by the Department towards 
promotion of basic, applied & clinical health  research and to ensure infrastructure for 
research work.  The Committee hopes that  all major schemes envisaged by the 
Department would be implemented and translated into action within the next six 
months.   
 
1.5        The Committee feels that for ensuring  translation of research there is a need to 
concentrate on taking research to its logica l conclusion in the fi eld of drugs, vaccines 
(both preventive and therapeutic) diagnosis, microbicides, vector and control products 
and platform technologies.  The Committee re commends that the Department should  
make all efforts for achieving the above objectives. 
 
1.6     The Committee further recommends that there is a need to put in place necessary 
framework and guidelines for research activitie s.  Ethical guidelines should be ensured 
through proper legislation, professional self-regulations and external bodies.  The 
priority areas should be identified and prior ity should be set for various aspects of the 
health research.  A National Health Resear ch Policy should be framed and a National 
Health Research Forum should be created  at the earliest.  Appropriate mechanism 
should be established for mapping and accred itation of Health Research Institutions.  
Besides, Knowledge Management Policy should be framed at the earliest. 
 
 
 

 8
II BUDGETARY ALLOCATION 
 
 
2.1 The Committee notes that out of total Elev enth Plan Outlay of Rs.4696.08 crore, only 
Rs.1496.49 crore  have been allocated for the first four years of the Plan  period which is 34 
percent of the total outlay.  The remaining ou tlay of Rs. 3199.51 crore is to be allocated and 
utilized in the final year of the Eleventh Plan period i.e. 2011-12.   
 
2.2 The Committee expresses its displeasure over the funds management of the 
Department.  Under no circumstances it coul d be possible for the Department to utilize 
66% of the total Plan outlay in the final year of the Eleventh Plan Period. 
 
2.3 As per the information furnished by the Department, the BE and RE allocations and 
the expenditure figures in respect thereof for 2008-09 and 2009-10 are as follows:

2.4 Total Budgetary allocation for the Department in BE 2010-11 is Rs. 660.00 crore out 
of which Rs. 500.00 crore is the plan comp onent and Rs. 160.00 crore is the non plan 
component.  The plan compon ent reflects an increase of  Rs. 100.00 crore over the RE 2009-
10 allocation. 
 
2.5 On being asked about the projections made by the Department for      2010-11, the 
Department has informed that against a proj ection of Rs. 1644.39 crore (Plan), provision of 
only Rs. 500.00 crore has been made.  The major programmes likely to be affected due to 
shortfall include the proposals to establish a network of virus diagnostic laboratories, 
establishment of facilities for health researc h in medical colleges and the establishment of 

 9
model rural health research units. Apart fr om this, funding of projects for product 
development in key areas is also likely to be affected. 
 
2.6 The Committee expresses its dissatisfacti on on such a big gap between the 
required and allocated funds.  The Committee notes that the major programmes likely to 
be affected as a result of the shortfall of Rs.1144.39 crores in plan allocation are 
establishment of network of virus diagnostic laboratories,  facilities for health research 
in medical colleges and model rural health re search units.  Prevalen ce of various virus 
infections like swine flue, dengue, Chikunguny a etc. is a very common feature in the 
country and large number of people suffer every year due to various viral infections.  
Presently there is acute shortage of virus diag nostic laboratories in the country and as a 
result of meagre plan allocation for 2010- 11, the effective control of various virus 
infection-related life threatening ailments wo uld be a distant dream.  Similarly, in the 
absence of adequate facilities for health research in medical colleges, the very purpose of 
coordination between the medical education and health research would be defeated.  
More than 70 per cent populat ion resides in the rural ar eas and as a result of non-
establishment of model rural health research units, the rural population of the country 
would be deprived of the critical health care facilities like disease diagnostics.   
 
2.7 The Committee views with serious concern that such critical areas of health 
research would be affected adversely due to resource crunch.  The Committee observes 
that scientific knowledge generated through h ealth and bio-medical research is used to 
develop drugs, diagnostics, devices and vaccine s that ultimately find place in the health 
system of the country.  The Committee, th erefore, recommends that the funds crunch 
should not be allowed to come  in the way of establishing a network of virus diagnostic 
laboratories, facilities for health research , model rural health research units and 
generation of new knowledge in such a crucial area as health research. 
 
 
2.8 The Committee also notes that the Planni ng Commission had allocated an amount 
of Rs. 800 crore for 2010-11 for the Department, which was subsequently reduced to Rs. 
500 without assigning any reason therefor.   Considering the fact that the Department 

 10
was specifically created to gi ve impetus to bio-medical res earch in the country, which is 
a sector that is very crucial to the health and well-being of the people of the country, the 
Committee is of the considered view that Rs. 500.00 crore will not be su fficient to fulfill 
the mandate of the Department. The Committee, therefore, recommends that allocation 
for the Department for this fiscal should  be increased to Rs. 800.00 crore, initially 
allocated by the Planning Commission.  
 
2.9 Though the Committee is all for enhanced a llocation for the Department, its scrutiny 
of various other Major Heads of Account has also revealed non-utilization of the entire 
budgeted allocation which is a matter of concern.  The Committee notes that funds 
allocated for the following schemes have remained unutilized during 2008-09 and 2009-10 
with only taken money spent in one or two schemes:-  
• Promotion, Coordination and Development of Basic, Applied and Clinical Research 
• Promotion and Guidance on Research Governance Issues 
• Inter-sectorial Coordination in Medical, Biomedical and Health 
• Advanced Training in Research in Medicine and Health 
• International Cooperation in Medical and Health Research 
• Matters relating to Epidemics, Natural Calamities and Develo pment of Tools to 
prevent outbreaks 
• Coordination in the field of Health Research with Governments, Organisations and 
Institutes  
 
2.10 Explaining the reasons behind non-ut ilization of budgeted funds during 2008—09, 
and 2009-10, the Department has stated that since the Department was notified only on 17
th 
September, 2007 and the work of the Departme nt commenced with the appointment of the 
first Secretary in November, 2008, the only on going scheme transferred to the Department 
was that relating to the ICMR. Although the responsibilities entrusted to the new 
Department were multiple, there were no matchi ng mechanisms or processes to undertake 
these schemes. In view of the above, all compon ents under heads other than ICMR  needed  
to be taken up as new initiatives. 
 
2.11 The Committee has also been informed that new schemes have been formulated 
over the last year so as to fulfil the mandat e and work entrusted to the Department. These 
proposals now require approval of the Pla nning Commission as well as other mandatory 

 11
clearances like SFC, EFC and CCEA.  Howeve r, with formulation of new schemes, the 
process has commenced for securing mandatory clearances to commence the scheme and it 
is anticipated that most of these will be launched in 2010-11. However, the final outcome 
will depend on the quantum of funding and the mandatory clearances. 
 
2.12 The Committee is constrained to note that funds amounting to Rs. 129.00 crore 
and Rs. 8.00 crore allocated in 2008-9 and 2009-10 respectively remained blocked 
presumably due to delay in approvals and non-finalization of plans/schemes. Rs. 83.00 
crore has been allocated for the above pr ojects for 2010-11. The Committee exhorts the 
Department to secure all mandatory clearances and initiate the implementation of the 
above projects so as to ensure optimum utilization of the allocated funds for 2010-11.   
 
2.13 The Committee notes that there is a huge mismatch between the projected 
demands by the Department and the approved BE for the year 2010-11.  The same was 
the trend in 2008-09 as well, when against the projected demand of Rs. 1613.00 crore on 
the plan side, the Department was allocate d Rs. 531.75 crore and the actual expenditure 
(plan) was Rs. 389.85 crore only. While the Co mmittee is supportive of the Department’s 
demand for higher allocation, it is, also, imperative on the part of the Department to take 
suitable measures to reverse this trend of  unrealistic projection of fund requirements 
and make its estimates only after proper assessment and planning. If the budget 
formulation is reduced to a ritualistic exer cise, it leads to under-utilization/non-
utilization of scare resources which a country like India can ill-afford. The Committee 
would  
 
 
therefore like to be apprised of the measures taken for objective and realistic 
formulation of the budget requirement of  the Department.  The Committee also 
recommends that the Department prepare a comprehensive action plan for optimal 
utilization of the funds, which should be revi ewed periodically by the Secretary of the 
Department.   
 

 12
2.14 The plan allocation for the North Eastern Areas in RE 2008-09 and RE 2009-10 was 
Rs. 40.00 crore each and the entire allocation wa s utilized during both the above years.  An 
allocation of Rs. 50.00 crore has been made in BE 2010-11.   
 
2.15 The Committee welcomes the enhanced allocation for the North Eastern Areas for 
2010-11, which is fully justified in view of the excellent track-record of the Region in the 
matter of utilization of the funds allocated in the past.  However the Committee would 
like to be enlightened as to whether the entire budget allocation was spent for the 
intended purposes during 2008-09 and 2009-10 or some part of it was transferred to the 
non-lapsable pool to be utilized later. 
 
 
III INDIAN COUNCIL OF MEDICAL RESEARCH   
 
3.1 The Indian Council of Medical Research is the apex body for the formulation, 
coordination and promotion of bio-medical and health research in the country. 
3.2 The Indian Council of Medical Researc h promotes biomedical research in the 
country through intramural as well as extramu ral research.  Intramural research is carried 
out currently through the Council's 29 Research Institutes/Centres/Units. These include (i) 
18 mission-oriented national institutes   located in different parts of India that address 
themselves to research on specific areas such as tuberculosis, leprosy, cholera and 
diarrhoeal diseases, viral diseases includin g AIDS, malaria, kala-azar, vector control, 
nutrition, reproduction, immunohaemat ology, oncology, medical statistics,  etc;  (ii) 6 
Regional Medical Research Centres
 that address regional health problems, and also aim to 
strengthen or generate research capabilities in different geographic areas of the country; 
and (iii)  5 Unit/Centres  dealing with food & drug toxicology, viral diseases, handling 
microorganisms of highly infectious nature, pr enatal diagnosis for  neonatal retardation etc 
and supply of various animal models an d feeds for experimental purposes.    
Extramural research  is promoted by ICMR through (i) Setting up Centres for Advanced 
Research in different research areas around existing expertise and infrastructure in selected

departments of Medical Colleges, Universities and other non-ICMR Research Institutes.(ii) 
Task force  studies which emphasise a time-bound, goal-oriented approach with clearly

aid received from scientists in non-ICMR Research Institutes, Medical colleges, Universities 
etc. located in different parts of the country.

XIII       HPV VACCINE 
 
13.1        During the interaction with th e Secretary, Health Research, his attention was 
drawn towards the ongoing trials of HPV vaccine on the children in Khammam district of 

 33
Andhra Pradesh and reported deaths of the child ren therefrom. Exact status in this regard 
was sought from the Secretary .  The Secretary, Department of Health Research informed 
the Committee that it was a vaccine against the Papilloma virus which causes cervical 
cancer in women.  The Drug Controller General  of India had given approval for marketing 
of HPV vaccine in India as a vaccine to be prescribed by the clinicians as per schedule ‘Y’ of 
the Drugs and Cosmetics Act and then a post -marketing surveillance.  The Committee was 
informed that the proposal for trial came tw o years back before the ICMR through PATH, 
an American NGO and the logic for allowing the trial was to see acceptability of this 
vaccine on Indian population.  Besides, these trials were approved by the National Ethical 
Committee and the State Ethical Committee.  Attention of the Secretary was drawn to 
DCGI guidelines whereunder third phase trial cannot be conducted on children until a 
similar trial was conducted on adults.  It wa s admitted by the Secr etary that the DCGI 
guidelines were not adhered to in the present case but this vaccine is given before the 
sexual activity begins and then it protects against cancer.  That was the reason for allowing 
trials on girls of the age of 10-14 year s.  The Committee was assured that State 
Governments of Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat wo uld be asked to get the ongoing clinical 
trial stopped immediately.   
 
13.2    Taking serious view of procedural and ethi cal lapses on the part of the Ministry, 
the Committee sought the matter of allowing trial of the vaccine as also the approval for 
its marketing in the country to be enquired into by a premier investigating agency and 
to take further appropriate follow-up action in  the matter.  It also asked that findings of 
the investigating agency and the follow-up ac tion taken in this regard may be furnished 
to the Committee at the earliest .  The Committee took a serious view in the matter and 
recommends the Department of Health Research  that in future all guidelines and norms 
should be adhered to before allowing trials of any drug including vaccines on Indian 
population.  The Committee also recommends th at the Drug Controller General of India 
should observe optimum precautions and follow all norms and guidelines while 
allowing marketing of any drug including the vaccines in the Indian market.

OBSERVATIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS   AT A GLANCE 
 
I. INTRODUCTION 
 The Committee appreciates the effort s made by the Department towards 
promotion of basic, applied & clinical health  research and to ensure infrastructure for 
research work.  The Committee hopes that  all major schemes envisaged by the 
Department would be implemented and translated into action within the next six 
months.  (Para 1.4) 
 
The Committee feels that for ensuring transl ation of research there is a need to 
concentrate on taking research to its logical conclusion in the fiel d of drugs, vaccines 
(both preventive and therapeutic) diagnosis, microbicides, vector and control products 
and platform technologies.  The Committee re commends that the Department should  
make all efforts for achieving the above objectives. (Para 1.5) 
 
The Committee further recommends that there is a need to put in place necessary 
framework and guidelines for research activitie s.  Ethical guidelines should be ensured 
through proper legislation, professional self-regulations and external bodies.  The 
priority areas should be identified and prior ity should be set for various aspects of the 
health research.  A National Health Resear ch Policy should be framed and a National 
Health Research Forum should be created  at the earliest.  Appropriate mechanism 
should be established for mapping and accred itation of Health Research Institutions.  
Besides, Knowledge Management Policy should be framed at the earliest. (Para 1.6) 
 
 
II BUDGETARY ALLOCATION 
 
The Committee expresses its displeasure over the funds management of the 
Department.  Under no circumstances it coul d be possible for the Department to utilize 
66% of the total Plan outlay in the final year of the Eleventh Plan Period. (Para 2.2) 
 
 
 The Committee expresses its dissatisfacti on on such a big gap between the 
required and allocated funds.  The Committee notes that the major programmes likely to 

 38
be affected as a result of the shortfall of Rs.1144.39 crores in plan allocation are 
establishment of network of virus diagnostic laboratories,  facilities for health research 
in medical colleges and model rural health re search units.  Prevalen ce of various virus 
infections like swine flue, dengue, Chikunguny a etc. is a very common feature in the 
country and large number of people suffer every year due to various viral infections.  
Presently there is acute shortage of virus diag nostic laboratories in the country and as a 
result of meagre plan allocation for 2010- 11, the effective control of various virus 
infection-related life threatening ailments wo uld be a distant dream.  Similarly, in the 
absence of adequate facilities for health research in medical colleges, the very purpose of 
coordination between the medical education and health research would be defeated.  
More than 70 per cent populat ion resides in the rural ar eas and as a result of non-
establishment of model rural health research units, the rural population of the country 
would be deprived of the critical health care facilities like disease diagnostics.  (Para 2.6) 
 
 The Committee views with serious concern that such critical areas of health 
research would be affected adversely due to resource crunch.  The Committee observes 
that scientific knowledge generated through h ealth and bio-medical research is used to 
develop drugs, diagnostics, devices and vaccine s that ultimately find place in the health 
system of the country.  The Committee, th erefore, recommends that the funds crunch 
should not be allowed to come  in the way of establishing a network of virus diagnostic 
laboratories, facilities for health research , model rural health research units and 
generation of new knowledge in such a crucial area as health research. (Para 2.7) 
 
 The Committee also notes that the Planni ng Commission had allocated an amount 
of Rs. 800 crore for 2010-11 for the Department, which was subsequently reduced to Rs. 
500 without assigning any reason therefor.   Considering the fact that the Department 
was specifically created to gi ve impetus to bio-medical res earch in the country, which is 
a sector that is very crucial to the health and well-being of the people of the country, the 
Committee is of the considered view that Rs. 500.00 crore will not be su fficient to fulfill 
the mandate of the Department. The Committee, therefore, recommends that allocation 

 39
for the Department for this fiscal should  be increased to Rs. 800.00 crore, initially 
allocated by the Planning Commission. (Para 2.8) 
 
 
 The Committee is constrained to note that funds amounting to Rs. 129.00 crore 
and Rs. 8.00 crore allocated in 2008-9 and 2009-10 respectively remained blocked 
presumably due to delay in approvals and non-finalization of plans/schemes. Rs. 83.00 
crore has been allocated for the above pr ojects for 2010-11. The Committee exhorts the 
Department to secure all mandatory clearances and initiate the implementation of the 
above projects so as to ensure optimum utilization of the allocated funds for 2010-11.  
(Para 2.12) 
 
 
 The Committee notes that there is a huge mismatch between the projected 
demands by the Department and the approved BE for the year 2010-11.  The same was 
the trend in 2008-09 as well, when against the projected demand of Rs. 1613.00 crore on 
the plan side, the Department was allocate d Rs. 531.75 crore and the actual expenditure 
(plan) was Rs. 389.85 crore only. While the Co mmittee is supportive of the Department’s 
demand for higher allocation, it is, also, imperative on the part of the Department to take 
suitable measures to reverse this trend of  unrealistic projection of fund requirements 
and make its estimates only after proper assessment and planning. If the budget 
formulation is reduced to a ritualistic exer cise, it leads to under-utilization/non-
utilization of scare resources which a country like India can ill-afford. The Committee 
would therefore like to be apprised of th e measures taken for objective and realistic 
formulation of the budget requirement of  the Department.  The Committee also 
recommends that the Department prepare a comprehensive action plan for optimal 
utilization of the funds, which should be revi ewed periodically by the Secretary of the 
Department.  (Para 2.13) 
 
 
 
 The Committee welcomes the enhanced allocation for the North Eastern Areas for 
2010-11, which is fully justified in view of the excellent track-record of the Region in the 

 40
matter of utilization of the funds allocated in the past.  However the Committee would 
like to be enlightened as to whether the entire budget allocation was spent for the 
intended purposes during 2008-09 and 2009-10 or some part of it was transferred to the 
non-lapsable pool to be utilized later. (Para 2.15) 
 
 
 
III INDIAN COUNCIL OF MEDICAL RESEARCH   
 
 The Committee notes that the shortfall between the amount allocated and the 
amount projected for ICMR is to the tune of Rs. 630.00 crore which is quite large by any 
standards and is certain to have an advers e bearing on the implementation of various 
research projects of ICMR.  The Committee observes that in view of the dynamic 
international health research environment a nd the current and future health challenges, 
the role of ICMR is very crucial and if its projects are plagued with under-funding, it can 
have very serious repercussions and undermine the desired outcomes in the health 
sector.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that more funds be allocated to ICMR.  
Simultaneously, the Committee impresses upon the ICMR, to exercise better fiscal 
discipline and take credible and tangible ac tion to improve the financial administration 
which will ultimately bolster its claims for more funds. (Para 3.7) 
 
 
 The Committee is happy to note the sterli ng achievements of ICMR and places on 
record its appreciation for the endeavors made  by it.   At the same time, the Committee 
would like to highlight two key concerns iden tified in the Eleventh Plan, i.e.(i) bridging 
the “Know-do” gap and (ii) delivery of the products of health research to the people who 
need it most. It has been observed that wh ile health research has made appreciable 
progress, there remains a time lag in translating the research outcome into tangible 
health products or in application of the kn owledge generated through research and that 
there is a need to mobilize research to brid ge the gap between what is known and what 
is done.  Equally important is to ensure that  the products of hea lth research reach and 
are used by the people who need it most.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that 

 41
the specific health products/processes accruing from each of the above 
innovations/achievements of ICMR should be introduced into public health service and 
be made accessible to all sections including th e most deprived sections of the society.  
The Committee would like to be kept apprised of the progress made in this regard. (Para 
3.14) 
 
 
 
 The Committee observes that health research projects funded with public money 
should be assessed in terms of tangible health outcomes for the masses and there should 
also be a mechanism for evaluating the hea lth benefits ensuing from such research 
projects.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that a system be put in place to do 
audit of health research being funded, who lly or partially, with government money, so 
that an assessment could be made as to whethe r or not the health research being done is 
justified and relevant. (Para 3.15)

proper implementation of all the activities co ntemplated under this Head.  Only then its 
demand for higher allocation at the RE stag e will have credibility.  The Committee also 
notes that mandatory clearances are yet to be obtained for the schemes/projects under 
this head.  While the Committee recommends that lack of funding should not be 
allowed to impact on the schemes under this  head, it also exhort s the Department to 
move forward towards initiating the process of obtaining necessary clearances.  (Para 
7.5) 
 
 The Committee would also like to be appris ed of the findings of the Expert Group 
constituted to identify the areas in which the Department of Health Research will 
complement the efforts of other science agencies. (Para 7.6) 
 
 
 
VIII INTERNATIONAL COOPERATION IN MEDICAL AND HEALTH RESEARCH 
 
 The Committee regrets to note that this is  yet another case of poor planning and 
unrealistic projections for allocation of f unds, leading not only to substantial under-
utilization of funds but also to the above programmes remaining non-starter.  
Notwithstanding substantial under utilization of funds in 2009-10, an enhanced 
allocation of Rs. 8.00 crore has been made in BE 2010-11.  The Committee exhorts the 
Department to prepare an action plan fo r optimum utilization of funds allocated for 
2010-11 under this head and also thrash out lingering issues, if any, expeditiously so as 
to commence the programmes without any further delay. (Para 8.4) 
  

 46
IX MATTERS RELATING TO EPIDE MICS, NATURAL CALAMITIES AND 
DEVELOPMENT OF TOOLS TO PREVENT OUTBREAKS. 
 
 The Committee observes that very important activities have been proposed under 
the above head.  However, merely conceptualizing the schemes on paper will not lead to 
anything if they are not operationalised within a specific time-frame. (Para 9.7) 
 
 The Committee notes that the plan funds to the tune of Rs. 1.00 crore were 
allocated for B.E 2009-10.  However, no expenditure was incurred under this head during 
2009-10 and the entire amount was surrendered.   The Committee expects that at least 
from this year onwards, the funds would be administered in a more diligent manner, 
making disaster management a more mean ingful exercise.  The Committee, therefore, 
recommends that the modalities for the schem es are finalised with fair amount of 
promptitude and mandatory clearances are obtained well in time.  The Committee 
would like to be apprised of the progress made towards implementation of the above 
programmes. (Para 9.8) 
 
 
X COORDINATION IN THE FIELD  OF HEALTH RESEARCH WITH 
GOVERNMENTS, ORGANIZATIONS AND INSTITUTES. 
 
 The Committee observes that there is huge mismatch between the projected 
demand of the Department and the allocated funds under this head for 2010-11.  The 
Committee also takes note of the submissi on by the Department that since these 
programmes have not commenced, utilizatio n was only Rs. 15.00 lakhs in 2009-10.  The 
Committee is constrained to observe that th e Department was not very prudent in its 
budget formulation. The Committee theref ore recommends that henceforth the 
Department should make its estimates only after proper assessment of actual 
requirement of funds under this head. (Para 10.3) 
 

 47
 The Committee notes the submission of the Department that it proposes to 
establish a mechanism for coordination and jo int funding of projects.  However, the 
only forward movement in this direction is the setting up of an apex Committee of 
Secretaries.  The Committee observes that there are a number of government 
organizations conducting research in various specific areas and therefore, creation of an 
institutional coordination mechanism is must for synergizing the core competencies of 
the different research organizations/agencies.  The Committee, therefore, recommends to 
the Department to urgently institutionalize the coordination mechanism. (Para 10.4) 
 
 The Committee would also like to be a pprised of the progress made towards 
developing the Guidelines for Coordination with other 
Departments/organisations/agencies. (Para 10.5) 
 
  The Committee also observes that very important activities are envisaged to be 
undertaken under this head.  However, the Committee is not aware of the roadmap for 
meaningful realization of the goals set under this head.  The Committee, therefore, 
recommends to the Department to draw up an  action plan in coordination with other 
organizations/agencies concerned to implemen t the projects envisaged under this head 
in a time-bound manner.  (Para 10.6) 
XI MATTERS RELATING TO SCIENTIF IC SOCIETIES AND ASSOCIATIONS, 
CHARITABLE AND RELIGIOUS ENDOWMENTS IN MEDICINE AND 
HEALTH RESEARCH AREAS. 
 
 The Committee deprecates the Department  for its inability to implement one 
project after another on time and projecting budgetary demands in an unrealistic 
manner.  This calls for serious introspectio n.  The Committee genuinely hopes that the 
projects envisaged under this head would commence during the current fiscal and 
exhorts the Department with all the power at its command to start the ground work for 
implementation of the programmes under this head in right earnest. (Para 11.3) 
  
XII PROVISION FOR PROJECTS/SCHEMES OF NORTH EASTERN AREAS AND 
SIKKIM 

 48
 
 The Committee notes that the ICMR’s Regional Medical Research Centre, 
Dibrugarh has been conducting research on various health issues/areas of special 
significance to the North Eastern Region, wh ich have provided significant leads.  The 
Committee also notes that during 2009-10, close to 90 studies were continued and several 
new studies have been initiated to address the major health concerns of North Eastern 
Region.  The Committee would like to be  apprised of the specific health 
products/processes that have been generated through the research activities/studies 
undertaken in the North Eastern Region and us ed for treatment of ailments specific to 
the people of the region. (Para 12.5) 
 
 
 
 The Committee is happy to note that there are two Committees, one each for 
review of extramural research and intramural research, in order to ensure that research 
projects are conducted in a timely fashion.  However, the Committee would like to be 
apprised of all the research projects sanctioned during 2008-09 and 2009-10 and the 
designated time-line for their implementation. The Committee would also like to be 
informed of the physical achievements of th e various on-going and new projects under 
this head during 2010-11. (Para.12.7) 
 
XIII       HPV VACCINE 
 
Taking serious view of proc edural and ethical lapses on  the part of the Ministry, 
the Committee sought the matter of allowing trial of the vaccine as also the approval for 
its marketing in the country to be enquired into by a premier investigating agency and 
to take further appropriate follow-up action in  the matter.  It also asked that findings of 
the investigating agency and the follow-up ac tion taken in this regard may be furnished 
to the Committee at the earliest .  The Committee took a serious view in the matter and 
recommends the Department of Health Research  that in future all guidelines and norms 
should be adhered to before allowing trials of any drug including vaccines on Indian 

 49
population.  The Committee also recommends th at the Drug Controller General of India 
should observe optimum precautions and follow all norms and guidelines while 
allowing marketing of any drug including the vaccines in the Indian market. (Para 13.2) 
 
XIV MANPOWER REQUIREMENTS FOR DHR AND ICMR 
 
 The Committee is surprised to note that  our premier institute in the field of 
medical research has been working with the minimum staff for all these years.  The very 
fact that not a single post has been created during the last 25 years confirms Committee’s 
concerns in this regard.  Not only this, a larg e number of posts, that too, in scientific and 
technical grade are lying vacant.  The Co mmittee is not aware since when such a 
situation has been continuing.  The Comm ittee can imagine the kind of work stress 
being faced by our scientists, specially dur ing the time of epidemic outbreaks.  The 
Committee recommends that all the existing va cant posts in ICMR should be filled up 
without any further delay.  All 500 posts of scientists and 1000 matching posts of 
research fellows and technical posts should be created at the earliest and filled up. This 
exercise needs to be carried out in a time- bound manner. It should be ensured that 
unduly long time is not taken in getting the posts created, followed by a protracted 
exercise of getting them filled up.  Similar concerted efforts would also be required for

role so that lack of specialized manpower does not hamper the crucial research activities, 
both ongoing and proposed. (Para 14.8)

PREFACE 
 I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and Family Welfare, 
having been authorized by the Committee to present the Re port on its behalf, do hereby present this Forty-second 
Report of the Committee on the Demand for Grants of the Department of AIDS Control, Ministry of Health and Family 
Welfare for the year 2010-11. 
2. The Committee considered the various documents and re levant papers received from the Department of AIDS 
Control, Ministry of Health and Family  Welfare and also heard the Secretary an d other officials of the Department on 
the said Demands for Grants (2010-11) in its meeting held on the 6th April, 2010. 
3.  The Committee considered the Draft Report and adopted the same in its meeting held on the 26th April, 2010. 
 
 
  AMAR  SINGH  
NEW DELHI; Chairman, 
26
th
 April, 2010 Department-related Parliamentary
